observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a small metal saucepan with a black handle sitting on a lit gas burner (blue flame with orange tips) on a white stove. A person's two hands enter the frame: one hand grips the pan's handle at the right, the other holds a black silicone spatula (red logo on the handle) whose head is inside the pan, stirring a partly set yellow egg mixture with visible curds and liquid. A pale marble-look countertop fills the background, with an unused burner grate to the left.
visible_changes: The spatula head moves continuously around the interior of the pan in a stirring/folding motion, shifting between the left, center, and right sides of the egg mixture across the frames.
The egg curds and liquid within the pan are displaced and folded by the spatula, changing their arrangement frame to frame while remaining a semi-liquid scrambled mixture.
The hand holding the spatula makes small positional adjustments (the handle angle and the visible portion of the handle change slightly), consistent with manual stirring rather than a fixed pose.
The hand on the pan handle stays gripping the handle throughout, with only minor shifts in posture.
The blue flame under the pan persists and flickers slightly in intensity/shape.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the egg mixture looked before this excerpt (whether it was just poured in) and whether it reaches fully cooked scrambled consistency after the last frame.
The cook's body, face, and any other utensils or ingredients not shown.
Whether the stirring continues or stops once the clip ends.
uncertain_details: The framing of the background shifts a little over the sequence, but it is unclear whether this is a small camera move (pan/tilt/zoom) or just the cook/pan repositioning; the change is minor.
The degree to which the eggs firm up over the excerpt is subtle and not clearly distinguishable from mere motion of the curds.
Exact identity of the spatula brand and pan material cannot be confirmed beyond appearance.
